Final Project \- Shader Terrain Editor

For this Shaders final project I decided to make a terrain editor. This terrain editor uses the editor interface that I've been building over the course of the term and includes a menu to adjust the noise type and change the effect the noise has on the terrain. There are 8 layers so you can stack different noises together. Each layer has a mask based on either the height or the slope of the surface at that point. There are a bunch of different noise options, all being generated on the fly in the shader. This means I can pick any location, and there are no repeating patterns like with a texture.  
For the fragment shader, I put together a gradient system where you can pick from eight different colors, and it will layer them smoothly with materials. At each step of the gradient, you can pick the height at which it starts as well as the color that is displayed. You can also pick from a drop-down of preset material types. Each material type is a different combination of specular, ambient, and shininess values. You can also pick from a preset list of colored ranges that I thought looked cool. The whole surface uses per-fragment lighting and normal calculation, so it is perfectly smooth and uses realistic lighting.  
The terrain object is just a grid in the scene, and you can pick from multiple grid resolutions to get a better look.
